title: Reward-hacking as equilibrium: testing the finite-evaluation prediction on a small judge-model setup

original_idea.body:
# Reward-Hacking as Equilibrium Under Finite Evaluation

Best-of-n against an LLM judge; vary evaluation budget, plot hacking rate vs budget.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: tests when reward hacking is rational under bounded evaluation, giving a budget-based mitigation lever.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Best-of-n against an LLM judge, no training; clear methodology.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Independent-friendly: open models/API judge, no training, fuzzy-reward eval valuable.

low_compute.reasoning: Best-of-n inference, one GPU, no training.

novelty.reasoning: The equilibrium paper is recent; an accessible empirical confirmation of the budget prediction may be partially open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Theory is recent; accessible empirical budget-dependence test may be open.
